name: Solitaire Grand Harvest
summary: Solitaire Grand Harvest is a card game where every level costs credits to enter, and a per-level stake multiplier scales the cost against everything the level can pay back at once, credits, gems, cookies, puzzle pieces and card pack quality. A seeded piggy bank fills with every level played, won or lost, and converts into a single purchase once full. Around the level loop sit four separate ordered reward tracks, a farm restoration project, a collectible card album, and a rotating set of thirty-minute timed offers, each pulling on the same handful of balances the level loop already produces.
teaser: One multiplier toggle on Solitaire Grand Harvest's pre-level screen raises the entry price and multiplies five separate payouts at once, credits, gems, cookies, puzzle pieces and pack quality.

observations.name: Terms of service and privacy notice acceptance
observations.observed: The first screen after download states that the terms of service and privacy notice have been updated, names a class action waiver and an arbitration clause, and states that continuing acknowledges having read the privacy notice. This appears before any gameplay or character. Whether acceptance is a tap on a button or implied by continuing isn't stated.

observations.name: Cross-app tracking permission request
observations.observed: Immediately after the terms screen, Solitaire Grand Harvest shows the system request to track activity across other companies' apps and websites, before the first level and before any explanation of what tracking is used for.

observations.name: Farm introduction and guide character
observations.observed: The app opens on a farmhouse, and a dog named Sam introduces himself as the player's first farm friend and invites them to play. Sam reappears throughout to announce rewards, point at buttons and comment on progress. The main screen later shows further characters along the level path.

observations.name: Returning-user login hint
observations.observed: On the first screen, a balloon rises from the settings button inviting a returning user to log in and restore progress. The hint is shown before the first level is played, and the same text stays attached to the settings button afterward.

observations.name: Guided first level
observations.observed: The first level opens with an arrow pointing at the cards and an instruction to tap a card one higher or one lower than the card at the bottom of the screen, completed by playing a run upward from four. Completion shows a level-complete screen paying 1,000 coins. The top of the screen shows 10,000 coins and three darkened stars before play begins, and each successful card play adds points.

observations.name: Pre-level screen introduced on the second level
observations.observed: Before level two, a pre-level screen appears with a wins multiplier reading times one, an info button, three locked power-up slots named for the levels that unlock them, a cost of 1,000, and a Play button. The info button explains that raising the multiplier means playing at higher stakes for bigger rewards, with level difficulty staying the same while cost and reward both rise. Tapping a locked slot names the power-up and what it does. The screen states that multipliers themselves unlock at level 25.

tags.name: Reward Multiplier
tags.rationale: Solitaire Grand Harvest pays a base reward for winning a level and lets the user raise it by a stated factor of two or four, with the info text stating that level difficulty stays the same while rewards are multiplied (tier: directly observed). The factor applies to credits and to the level's other rewards, which rise from one to two to four cookies and puzzle pieces and from a green to a blue to a purple pack, and the narrator reports the doubled payout after a level (tier: directly observed). The higher factor is bought with a higher entry cost in credits (tier: directly observed). The timed offer's "ten percent more gems for fifteen minutes" is a stated additive modifier over the gems a level already pays (tier: directly observed, offered but not bought).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Boosters. The multiplier is set on the pre-level screen as a stake rather than held and expended as an item, and it changes the payout rather than the level's conditions, which the entry places under this tag (tier: directly observed).

tags.name: Progression Gate
tags.rationale: Solitaire Grand Harvest states the player level at which power-ups, multipliers, My Trail, the Social Hub, the Grand Album, stats and teams become available, shows them as unavailable below that level, and opens them on reaching it (tier: directly observed). The farm withholds areas until the farm level rises and opened the tool shed at farm level two (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Milestone for the unlock moments. The level requirement is a standing state shown before it is met, which this entry covers; the unlock recognitions are covered by Milestone only where a separate reward event occurs (tier: directly observed).

observations.name: Forced continuation and escape routes during early guidance
observations.observed: After early levels the app moves the player straight into the next level without showing the level path, though an X button allows leaving to look around the farm. After the first harvest tutorial, the app states that the player should tap to start the next level, and that screen cannot be declined, though the following introduction screen can then be closed with X. After closing, Sam lists the next unlocks: the Grand Album, My Trail and the Social Hub, each at a named level.

observations.name: Starting balance and the introduction of credits
observations.observed: The player starts with 10,000 coins. After level three and the first daily reward, a pop-up introduces credits as a second thing to use for playing levels and getting power-ups, and grants 10,000 credits. Why this particular grant of 10,000 credits was made isn't stated. Coins, gold and credits are used for what appears to be the same balance, though which of these are the same balance and which are separate isn't fully settled.

observations.name: Profile and avatar selection
observations.observed: The main screen shows a blank default avatar; tapping it opens a profile where the player can choose a mouse, a dog or a cat as their picture, or connect Facebook. The profile shows the player's join year, level, and crop number, alongside an Info and Stats tab. Tapping the profile photo itself does nothing; tapping an animal changes it. A pointer later appears on the avatar suggesting new avatars are available, regardless of what the player has already chosen.

observations.name: Solitaire level rules
observations.observed: Each level is a solitaire layout in which the player plays face-up cards one higher or one lower than the current base card, drawing a new base card from the deck when no card is playable. A level is won when the layout is cleared, and up to three stars are awarded, with unused cards from the extra stack counting toward the star bar. A level win pays credits, a larger amount on the first level and a smaller amount on later levels relative to their entry cost.

observations.name: Level obstacles and new card types introduced across levels
observations.observed: Later levels add obstacles and card types, each introduced with its own explanatory card: a mouse that must collect cheese pieces to reveal cards underneath, a squirrel that collects nuts, purple cards that add extra cards to the deck when revealed, and a card whose value changes after every move. Gem cards appear once the farm is introduced, with collected gems flying to a basket. A different layout, scrolling left to right, is used in the gem tutorial level.

observations.name: Per-level entry cost in credits
observations.observed: Starting a level costs credits: 1,000 at the base multiplier, 3,000 at the doubled multiplier and 6,000 at the four-times multiplier, with the pre-level screen stating the cost and the info text stating that cost rises with each multiplier. One level was shown with a stated reduction in cost, without an explanation. A held free round can be used in place of the cost. Whether a balance below the entry cost blocks play isn't shown.

The background music changes with the selection, and some events are available only in one-times mode.

observations.observed: When the player skips a playable card, Solitaire Grand Harvest shows a message offering to undo the miss. The prompt appeared at least twice, and wasn't used the second time. Undo is a held item granted in rewards and bundles.

Scrolling the main screen early on shows a message naming a large number of games remaining before the next crop unlocks, which doesn't match a later message naming only five levels remaining.

Crop Master is reached after level 46.

systemView: Solitaire Grand Harvest is a complex system. Its spine is credits: every level costs credits to enter, and the multiplier chosen before a level scales both that cost and every reward the level pays at once, credits, gems, cookies, puzzle pieces and pack quality, so the whole economy moves on one per-level decision.

mechanicWriteups.name: Piggy Bank
mechanicWriteups.summary: Peggy fills with a bonus deposit after every level played, won or lost, seeded by the app itself, and converts into a single 3.99 purchase once capped.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Peggy is introduced with a first deposit the app makes itself, described as "on us," and grows after every level played regardless of whether the level is won or lost. The balance rises from 4,050 credits through 7,000 and 21,000 to a cap of 35,000, at which point Solitaire Grand Harvest states that no more credits can be collected until the savings are claimed, priced at 3.99 with a two-day timer.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Peggy sits behind the barn as a pig icon that jumps across the screen after each completed level, visibly growing fatter as the balance rises. Once capped, Peggy takes over the same top-right offer slot the expired timed offers occupied.
mechanicWriteups.noting: The first deposit coming from the app itself, not from anything the player did, sets up the reserve as something already owned before a single purchase prompt appears; by the time the cap message shows, the credits inside read as the player's own money waiting to be unlocked rather than a fresh sale.
findings: Peggy's first deposit of 4,050 credits is made by the app itself.
The balance grows after every level played, won or lost.
Peggy caps at 35,000 credits and then blocks further deposits until claimed.
Claiming the capped balance costs 3.99 under a two-day timer.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: Peggy at an early balance growing after a level; the capped "maxed out" message with its price and timer.

mechanicWriteups.name: Reward Multiplier
mechanicWriteups.summary: A single one, two or four times toggle on the pre-level screen sets that level's entry cost and multiplies its credit payout, gem yield, cookie and puzzle-piece count, and card pack tier together.
mechanicWriteups.observed: From level 25, the pre-level screen offers a stake choice between one, two and four times wins. Choosing a higher stake raises the entry cost in credits and multiplies what the level pays out: cookies and puzzle pieces rise from one to two to four, and the card pack awarded rises from green to blue to purple. The app's own text states that level difficulty stays the same while rewards are multiplied.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The choice sits directly on the pre-level screen alongside the entry cost, framed as "bigger prizes are available," and the background music changes with the selection, more upbeat at higher stakes and a falling tone when switching back to one times.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Tying pack color, and not just the credit payout, to the stake turns the multiplier into the single lever that also controls collection progress, so choosing to bet bigger is also a choice about how fast the album fills.
findings: The multiplier offers one, two or four times, raised from the pre-level screen.
A higher stake raises the entry cost in credits and multiplies the credit payout equally.
Cookies, puzzle pieces and card pack tier all scale with the same stake choice.
A timed offer separately sells a temporary ten percent bonus over the gems a level already pays.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: The pre-level screen's multiplier toggle with its stated cost at each tier; the three pack colors awarded at each multiplier.

mechanicWriteups.name: Boosters
mechanicWriteups.summary: Slicer, Windmill and Wild Drop power-ups plus held undos, wild cards and plus-five stacks each change what happens inside a level once applied, arriving through rewards, level gifts and paid bundles.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Solitaire Grand Harvest holds the Slicer, Windmill and Wild Drop power-ups as counted quantities, each introduced with a free first try: the Slicer removes cards at the start of a level, the Windmill clears face-up cards, and Wild Drop hides wild cards in the deck. Separately, undos, wild cards and plus-five card stacks are granted through daily rewards, level gifts, trail and puzzle rewards, and store bundles, each usable inside a level in progress.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Power-ups unlock one at a time at stated levels, each introduced with its own free trial before the player is asked to hold a count of their own. Held items surface inside a level at the moment they apply, an undo prompt after a missed card, a held free round offered in place of a level's cost.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Granting the first use of each power-up free, before any purchase is possible, lets the player learn what an item does before it becomes something to manage as a held count.
findings: Slicer, Windmill and Wild Drop each unlock with a free first use before becoming a held item.
Undos, wild cards and plus-five stacks arrive through rewards, level gifts, trail and puzzle prizes, and paid bundles.
Periods of endless windmill or infinite wild cards suspend the held count for a set number of minutes.
Whether using a held item reduces its count isn't stated.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: The locked power-up slots with their level requirements; a level showing a held undo or wild card offered mid-play.

mechanicWriteups.name: Hard Currency
mechanicWriteups.summary: Credits, gems, free rounds and puzzle pieces are all sold directly for money, in the Grand Harvest Store and inside a rotating set of thirty-minute timed offers.
mechanicWriteups.observed: The Grand Harvest Store sells credits in plain amounts and in bundles that also include free rounds, undos and wild cards, with prices from 1.99 up to 35.99. From level 36 the bundles add card packs at rising tiers. Gems appear in a paid timed offer of 300 for a stated price, and puzzle pieces are sold ten at a time for 0.99.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The store opens from tapping the credits balance directly, while the timed offers cycle through the top right corner of the main screen on a thirty-minute countdown, each capped at one purchase.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Four different balances being sold through the same store and offer surfaces, at prices that vary between the plain bundles and the timed offers for what reads as a similar amount, makes the actual credits-per-dollar rate hard to compare from one offer to the next.
findings: Credits are sold in plain amounts and in bundles from 1.99 to 35.99.
Card packs are added to store bundles from level 36 onward.
Gems are sold in a 300-gem timed offer, and puzzle pieces ten for 0.99.
Free rounds are included inside paid bundles and offers rather than sold on their own.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: The Grand Harvest Store's bundle tiers; a timed offer showing its countdown and one-purchase limit.

mechanicWriteups.name: Soft Currency
mechanicWriteups.summary: Credits, gems, free rounds, puzzle pieces and cookies are each earned through ordinary play, credits from level wins and a wide set of free rewards, the rest from levels and events tied to them.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Credits are paid by level wins, level gifts, daily rewards, the hourly harvest, trail rewards and set rewards, and spent on level entry and continuation. Gems are collected from gem cards inside levels and spent on farm tasks. Free rounds are granted by daily rewards and level gifts and exchanged for a level's entry cost. Puzzle pieces and cookies are paid by level wins and spent on the Grand Puzzle and on feeding the pet.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Each balance is earned as a side effect of playing rather than through a dedicated collection action, credits and gems from cards inside the level itself, cookies and puzzle pieces from the level's completion screen.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Five separate balances all being funded by the same handful of actions, playing a level and completing an event, means a single won level can move several counters at once without the player choosing to work toward any of them individually.
findings: Credits are earned from level wins, gifts, daily rewards, the hourly harvest, and trail and set rewards.
Gems are earned only from gem cards inside levels.
Free rounds, puzzle pieces and cookies are each earned through level wins and event rewards.
Crowns are stated to come from duplicate album cards, though none were earned or spent.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: A level's completion screen showing several balances updating at once; the farm's gem-cost task list.

mechanicWriteups.name: Loot Box
mechanicWriteups.summary: A second, paid lucky wheel spin and the card packs sold in the store from level 36 onward both resolve only after payment, over a materially different, undisclosed set of prizes.
mechanicWriteups.observed: After a free wheel spin, the wheel offers a second spin for 2.99 over a higher set of prizes, resolved only once the price is paid. From level 36, store bundles include purple, silver and gold card packs whose contents, based on packs already seen opening from level wins, vary and can repeat.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The paid spin appears immediately after the free one, with the wheel itself turning gold to mark the higher stakes; the store's packs sit priced alongside plain credit bundles with no odds shown for either.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Placing the paid spin directly after the free one, over a visibly richer prize set, uses the free draw's own suspense to introduce the paid version before the player has left the screen.
findings: The paid wheel spin costs 2.99 and resolves only after payment.
The second wheel's prizes are higher than the free spin's own set.
Store card packs from level 36 onward are also priced and resolved after purchase.
No odds or contents are disclosed for either the paid spin or the store packs.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: The paid wheel spin's prize set and price; a store bundle showing its card pack tier.

mechanicWriteups.name: Variable Reward Outcome
mechanicWriteups.summary: The free first wheel spin, packs won from levels, the Crop Master apple pick and the pet's birthday spin each resolve to one of several different results at no cost to draw.
mechanicWriteups.observed: A free wheel spin resolves to one of several prizes shown on the wheel face. Packs won from levels are opened with their cards revealed one by one, and cards differ between packs. The Crop Master pick offers four prizes hidden under twenty apples, and the pet's first-stage spin resolves to a pack from a wheel stated to pay up to 3,000 credits.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Each of these sits at the end of an activity already completed, winning a level, finishing a crop, completing a pet stage, rather than being something bought outright.
mechanicWriteups.noting: None of these four require the player to pay before the draw resolves, which is what keeps them apart from the paid wheel spin and store packs that sell the same suspense for money.
findings: The free wheel spin resolves to one of several displayed credit or item prizes.
Packs won from levels reveal different cards each time, including duplicates.
The Crop Master pick hides four prizes under twenty apples.
The pet's birthday spin resolves to a pack from a wheel stated to pay up to 3,000 credits.

mechanicWriteups.name: Set Collection
mechanicWriteups.summary: The twelve-set Grand Spring Album and the five-piece Grand Emblems case each track named collectible members toward a completion prize, filled by packs won in levels and by separate timed events.
mechanicWriteups.observed: The Grand Spring Album holds twelve sets of twelve cards, shows a completion percentage, and pays a reward for each finished set and a 610,000-credit grand prize for the whole album. Grand Emblems tracks five named emblems, each found in its own special event, toward a final prize on a countdown.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The album opens from level 36 with a welcome gift and fills as packs are won and opened; Grand Emblems is introduced as its own pop-up naming all five emblems and the prize for completing the set.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Running two separate collections side by side, one filled by ordinary level play and one filled only by taking part in specific timed events, gives the player two different reasons to chase the same kind of completion prize at once.
findings: The Grand Spring Album holds twelve sets of twelve cards each.
Completing all twelve sets pays a 610,000-credit grand prize.
Grand Emblems tracks five named emblems, each earned from a different special event.
Duplicate album cards are stated to convert into crowns, redeemable at the Crown Center.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: The album showing its set completion percentage; the Grand Emblems case with its five named pieces.

mechanicWriteups.name: Seasonal Progression Pass
mechanicWriteups.summary: My Trail, the Bloomlight Garden season, the Grand Puzzle and the pet track are four separate ordered reward tracks, each with its own countdown and its own by-product of play advancing it.
mechanicWriteups.observed: My Trail is a ten-position reward track ending in a mystery door, advanced by energy from missions, on a three-day countdown. The Bloomlight Garden season runs twelve chapters advanced by gem-paid tasks. The Grand Puzzle reveals a picture over a three-day window as pieces are placed. The pet progresses through five stages advanced by feeding it cookies, on a ten-day timer.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Each track sits on its own icon on the main screen with its own countdown, introduced separately as the player reaches the level that opens it.
mechanicWriteups.noting: None of the four tracks reaches its own end anywhere in what's covered here, so whether a track resets, closes, or opens something further when it ends isn't shown.
findings: My Trail runs ten reward positions to a mystery door on a three-day countdown.
The Bloomlight Garden season runs twelve chapters advanced by gem-paid tasks.
The Grand Puzzle runs three days and reopens for a second round once solved.
The pet runs five stages advanced by feeding, on a ten-day timer.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: My Trail's ten-position reward track; the Bloomlight Garden season's chapter and task screen.

mechanicWriteups.name: Challenge
mechanicWriteups.summary: The ten-minute balloon bonus and the five-level Cheese Rally race each set a bounded objective inside a short window, won or lost within that window rather than carried forward.
mechanicWriteups.observed: A floating balloon offers a prize for completing one task within the next ten minutes. Cheese Rally asks the player to be first to finish five Solitaire levels against four named racers, paying the winner and advancing to a further stage; a later race was not completed in time.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The balloon appears as a floating icon over the farm; Cheese Rally runs from its own event icon with a visible timer and the racers' relative progress.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Cheese Rally being available in one-times mode only ties a competitive, time-boxed objective to the lowest-stake way of playing, keeping the race separate from the multiplier decisions the rest of the economy runs on.
findings: The balloon bonus sets one task to complete within ten minutes.
Cheese Rally asks for five won levels before four named racers, within a timed window.
A won race advances to a further stage; a later race was not completed.
Cheese Rally is available only in one-times mode.

mechanicWriteups.name: Comparative Rank
mechanicWriteups.summary: Cheese Rally orders the player against four named racers by progress toward five won levels, deciding who reaches the stage prize first.
mechanicWriteups.observed: During Cheese Rally the player's position updates against four named racers as levels are won, moving from second to first before winning the first race.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Position is shown live during the race itself, tied to the same progress bar that tracks levels won toward the five needed to finish.
mechanicWriteups.noting: What's shown is the player's own position changing, not an ordered list of every racer's standing, so what a racer sees of anyone but themselves and the leader isn't shown.
findings: Position updates live against four named racers during Cheese Rally.
The player moved from second to first before winning the race.
Whether the racers are other players or automated entrants isn't stated.

mechanicWriteups.name: Daily Login Rewards
mechanicWriteups.summary: Daily Goodies pays a four-week sequence of rewards for visiting once a day, framed entirely around the visit itself rather than any action taken once inside.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Daily Goodies shows a four-week reward sequence and states that a daily visit sends bigger prizes. The first day paid 2,500 credits and six undos after level three; a later return, following a restart of the phone, paid day two's reward of 5,000 credits and three free rounds.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The sequence pops up with Sam on open, showing the full four weeks of rewards at once rather than only the day in question.
mechanicWriteups.noting: The daily farm delivery bonus reads like a second daily reward alongside this one, but it isn't part of it: what actually qualifies a visit for the farm bonus beyond completing farm tasks is never shown, so the two are kept separate rather than folded into one daily system.
findings: Daily Goodies shows a four-week sequence of daily rewards.
Day one paid 2,500 credits and six undos.
Day two paid 5,000 credits and three free rounds on the next visit.
Whether a missed day affects the sequence isn't stated.

mechanicWriteups.name: Streak
mechanicWriteups.summary: A bones meter fills with consecutive won levels in the same run of play and is separately kept in the profile as the longest win streak reached.
mechanicWriteups.observed: A pop-up introduces a bones meter beside Sam that fills toward extra prizes as levels are won in a row. The profile's stats tab separately records the longest win streak reached.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The meter sits on the main screen next to Sam once unlocked, filling visibly after each won level.
mechanicWriteups.noting: What a lost level does to the meter, and what the completed meter actually pays, are both left unshown, so only the existence of the streak and its record in the profile can be stated with confidence.
findings: The bones meter fills with consecutive won levels.
The profile records the longest win streak separately.
What a loss does to the meter isn't stated.
What filling the meter pays isn't stated.

mechanicWriteups.name: Progression Gate
mechanicWriteups.summary: Player level and farm level each withhold a named set of features, power-ups, multipliers, My Trail, the Social Hub, the Grand Album and teams, stated and shown as locked before the level is reached.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Solitaire Grand Harvest names the player level at which power-ups, multipliers, My Trail, the Social Hub, the Grand Album, further stats and teams open, and shows each as unavailable below that level. The farm withholds areas until its own separate level rises, opening the tool shed at farm level two.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Locked features are named ahead of time rather than hidden entirely, the Grand Album shows "Soon" before level 36, and locked power-up slots state the level that opens them.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Naming every gate's requirement well before the player reaches it turns the level path itself into a preview of what's still ahead, rather than each unlock arriving as a surprise.
findings: Power-ups, multipliers, My Trail and the Social Hub each unlock at a named player level.
The Grand Album shows a "Soon" state before opening at level 36.
The farm withholds areas until its own separate farm level rises.
Teams sits behind a level gate that stays closed throughout.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: A locked power-up slot naming its unlock level; the Grand Album's "Soon" state before level 36.

mechanicWriteups.name: Leveling
mechanicWriteups.summary: The player's level and the farm's separate level each hold a current position that a stated rule advances, and both are the measures the app's own gates read.
mechanicWriteups.observed: The farm holds a level raised by XP from completed tasks, announced as "we're level one" and then level two. The player's own level is kept as a profile state, shown as "level 2, crop 1" early and rising through play, and is the measure named on every progression gate.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The player's level is shown on the profile and used throughout as the unlock measure; the farm's level is shown separately on the farm screen itself, tied to task completion rather than to Solitaire play.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Running two separate level states, one from playing Solitaire and one from spending gems on farm tasks, means the game tracks two distinct kinds of progress that happen to share the same word.
findings: The farm holds its own level, raised by completing gem-paid tasks.
The player's level is a separate profile state, shown alongside a crop number.
The player's level is the measure every progression gate reads.
The farm's level opened the tool shed at farm level two.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: The profile showing the player's level and crop number; the farm screen showing its own level state.

mechanicWriteups.name: Experience Points
mechanicWriteups.summary: Farm tasks pay XP toward the farm's next level, and My Trail's missions pay energy toward its ten reward positions, each converting ordinary play into movement along its own track.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Completing farm tasks pays XP, stated directly as "earn XP by completing tasks," which raises the farm's level. My Trail is separately advanced by energy paid out from three rotating missions, each with its own counted objective and a refresh countdown.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Farm XP is shown only through the task manager's own completion percentage; trail energy has its own bar on My Trail's own screen, filled as each mission is completed.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Naming the trail's resource "energy" invites confusion with a capacity that limits play, but this energy only fills toward rewards and is never spent or depleted, which keeps it apart from anything that blocks or rations how much the player can do.
findings: Farm tasks pay XP that raises the farm's level.
My Trail's energy comes from three rotating missions, each paying a different amount.
Missions refresh and are replaced once completed.
Trail energy fills toward rewards and is never spent or depleted.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: The farm task manager showing its completion percentage; My Trail's mission list and energy bar.

mechanicWriteups.name: Milestone
mechanicWriteups.summary: Reaching level 10, 25 and 50 is recognized with its own congratulation and a gift held apart from the level's ordinary win reward.
mechanicWriteups.observed: At levels 10, 25 and 50 Solitaire Grand Harvest congratulates the player on the level reached and grants a gift on top of anything the level itself paid for winning: 1,000 credits, a free round and two undos at level 10, and 3,000 credits, a free round and two undos at level 25.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The gift screen arrives immediately on completing the level in question, separate from and following the ordinary level-complete screen.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Placing the level 10 gift directly before the app's own rating prompt uses the goodwill of an unexpected extra reward as the lead-in to asking for a rating.
findings: Levels 10, 25 and 50 each carry their own congratulation and gift.
The level 10 gift pays 1,000 credits, a free round and two undos.
The level 25 gift pays 3,000 credits, a free round and two undos.
The level 50 gift's contents aren't stated.

mechanicWriteups.name: Referral
mechanicWriteups.summary: An invite link ties a reward to a friend joining and reaching level 15, credited to the inviting user once that happens.
mechanicWriteups.observed: An invite card offers a generated link to send, stating that rewards follow once invited friends reach level 15. The reward itself is described only as "amazing rewards," with no further detail given.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The invite card appears in the corner of the main screen after level 20, framed around a friend count that already shows one of the two invites as filled before anyone is invited.
mechanicWriteups.noting: The reward's form is never named at any point the invite is shown, so what a successful referral actually pays stays undisclosed even as the invite itself is repeated.
findings: The invite link pays the inviting user once a friend reaches level 15.
The reward is described only as "amazing rewards," with no amount or item named.
The invite card counts one of two friend slots as already filled.
No invitation was sent.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: The invite friends card with its level-15 condition and generated link.

mechanicWriteups.name: Cosmetic Customization
mechanicWriteups.summary: The profile picture, the farm's name and the pet's name are presentation choices made once during first-run introductions, with no stated effect on play.
mechanicWriteups.observed: The player chooses a mouse, dog or cat as a profile picture, kept once applied. The farm and the pet are each named by the player when first introduced, with a default name offered for the pet.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Each choice is made once, at the moment the relevant feature is introduced, Sam's early tour for the profile picture, the farm's restoration intro for its name, the pet's hatching for its name.
mechanicWriteups.noting: None of these choices carries any stated effect on how a level plays, keeping them apart from anything that changes the game rather than how it presents the player back to themselves.
findings: The profile picture is chosen from a mouse, dog or cat.
The farm is named by the player during its introduction.
The pet is named by the player when it hatches, with a default name offered.
No functional effect on play is stated for any of these choices.

sectionLeadIns.onboarding: Solitaire Grand Harvest runs through a terms screen and a tracking request before a guided first level, then introduces a second balance, credits, within the first few levels.
sectionLeadIns.core-loop: Each level in Solitaire Grand Harvest is a solitaire layout that costs credits to enter, played by moving cards one higher or one lower than a base card, with power-ups, a streak meter and a stake multiplier all sitting around that same core action.
sectionLeadIns.goals: Levels sit on a path that grows crops in sequence, with fixed-level gifts, a win-streak meter and profile stats layered around that same path, and a separate set of tracks, Crop Master, My Trail, the farm and the album, each running its own progression alongside it.
sectionLeadIns.access: Player level and farm level each withhold a named set of features until a stated threshold, and a small number of modes and level types carry their own separate conditions.
sectionLeadIns.economy: Solitaire Grand Harvest runs six separate balances, credits, gems, free rounds, puzzle pieces, cookies and crowns, most of them earned through ordinary play and several of them also sold for money.
sectionLeadIns.social: Solitaire Grand Harvest's social surfaces are thin: a friends tab, a team feature behind a level gate, a card-trading notice with no surface behind it, and a race against named characters.
sectionLeadIns.reach: Settings offers sign-in through three services, an invite link sends a reward outside the app, and a newsletter sign-up is the first request for an email address encountered.
sectionLeadIns.monetization: Solitaire Grand Harvest's monetization runs through a store, a rotating set of timed offers, a piggy bank, a second paid wheel spin and a small puzzle-piece sale, all selling into the same handful of balances.
sectionLeadIns.returns: Solitaire Grand Harvest brings the player back on three separate clocks, daily, hourly and three-hourly, alongside a notification prompt and a set of multi-day event countdowns.

proposedTags.name: Interval Claim
proposedTags.draftDefinition: An interval claim is a free benefit that the product makes claimable again after a fixed interval of real time has passed since the last claim, shows the time remaining until the next claim, and grants nothing until the user returns and collects it.
proposedTags.conditions: A stated interval shorter than a day (one hour for the harvest, three hours for cookies); a visible countdown to the next claim; a claim action in the product; a benefit paid into a balance the product maintains.
proposedTags.whyNotCovered: Passive Construction requires a persistent entity that moves from a pre-construction state to a completed state through an active construction instance that advances without repeated input. The harvest timer builds nothing: when it runs out, the existing crops can be harvested again for credits, and neither the crops nor the farm change state. The entry's exclusions name both halves of this case: an existing structure that passively generates resources with no construction under way, and a timer that only delays reuse without creating or upgrading a persistent entity. The crops themselves grow through level completion (O16), not through the timer, and the cookie bonus (O64) has no entity at all. Daily Login Rewards requires a reward created by accessing the product within a defined daily window, limited to one entitlement per window, with a new opportunity at the daily reset. Here the qualifying condition is elapsed time since the last claim rather than access within a day, which the entry excludes; the harvest pays every hour and the cookie bonus every three hours, so several claims fall in one day, which the entry's daily claim limit also excludes; and both countdowns were observed starting at the claim (the cookie countdown read two hours fifty-nine minutes directly after it), which points to a clock that restarts from the last claim rather than a daily boundary. What the two share is a claimable reward that recurs; what Daily Login Rewards defines is a calendar of daily windows, and even a wall-clock version of these timers would run on intervals shorter than a day, which that entry does not cover. Energy covers a capacity consumed by actions, and nothing is consumed here. Daily / Weekly Quests requires an objective beyond returning.
proposedTags.recurrenceElsewhere: Timed free collections of this kind are common in mobile games, such as resource collectors and free chests on timers; the pattern can be described without reference to Solitaire Grand Harvest.
proposedTags.caveat: This proposal is held open. The split that decides its shape was not observed: whether unclaimed benefits accumulate across intervals up to a cap while the user is away, or whether the claim pays once and then waits until it is collected. A timer that pays once and waits is a different mechanic from one that banks up to a cap during absence, and the definition above cannot be settled until one of them is shown. Two kinds of evidence would settle it: a session that leaves the app for longer than several intervals and then returns to the harvest or the cookie bonus, or a second app carrying the same shape in which the accumulation rule is visible.

system.tagline: A card game where one per-level stake decision scales every balance the economy runs on at once.
system.overview: Solitaire Grand Harvest is a complex system built around credits: every level costs credits to enter, and the multiplier chosen before a level scales both that cost and every reward the level pays at once, credits, gems, cookies, puzzle pieces and pack quality. A seeded piggy bank fills with every level played, won or lost, and converts into a single purchase once full. Around the level loop sit four separate ordered reward tracks, a farm restoration project, a collectible card album and a rotating set of timed offers, each pulling on the same handful of balances the level loop already produces.
system.loop: The core loop is: choose a stake multiplier → play a level, spending credits to enter → win credits, gems, cookies, puzzle pieces and a card pack, all scaled by the chosen stake → feed those balances into farm tasks, the album, My Trail and the pet → let Peggy the piggy bank fill from every level played → claim the daily, hourly and three-hourly free rewards → spend on continuation cards, power-ups, or the store's bundles and timed offers when a balance runs short.
system.keyInsight: Credits are the connective tissue here: the reward multiplier scales what every level pays into the same balance, that balance feeds the piggy bank on every play whether the level is won or lost, and a paid route sits directly behind the balance running short, continuation cards, the store, and Peggy's own claim price. Nineteen published mechanics all draw on or feed back into the same handful of currencies, so a single won level can move several of them at once without the player choosing to work toward any of them individually.
system.whatMakesItWork: The system works because nearly every mechanic is priced in a currency the level loop already produces, not in a separate resource the player has to seek out. Boosters, the album, the farm, My Trail and the pet all draw on credits, gems, cookies or puzzle pieces the level loop pays automatically, so playing levels alone keeps every track moving, and the timed offers and Peggy's own claim price are simply where real money buys the same balances faster.

roles.role: Credits, gems, free rounds, puzzle pieces and cookies are each earned through ordinary play, credits from level wins and a wide set of free rewards, the rest from levels and events tied to them.
Credits, gems, free rounds and puzzle pieces are all sold directly for money, in the Grand Harvest Store and inside a rotating set of thirty-minute timed offers.
A single one, two or four times toggle on the pre-level screen sets that level's entry cost and multiplies its credit payout, gem yield, cookie and puzzle-piece count, and card pack tier together.
Peggy fills with a bonus deposit after every level played, won or lost, seeded by the app itself, and converts into a single 3.99 purchase once capped.
Slicer, Windmill and Wild Drop power-ups plus held undos, wild cards and plus-five stacks each change what happens inside a level once applied, arriving through rewards, level gifts and paid bundles.
A second, paid lucky wheel spin and the card packs sold in the store from level 36 onward both resolve only after payment, over a materially different, undisclosed set of prizes.
The free first wheel spin, packs won from levels, the Crop Master apple pick and the pet's birthday spin each resolve to one of several different results at no cost to draw.
The twelve-set Grand Spring Album and the five-piece Grand Emblems case each track named collectible members toward a completion prize, filled by packs won in levels and by separate timed events.
My Trail, the Bloomlight Garden season, the Grand Puzzle and the pet track are four separate ordered reward tracks, each with its own countdown and its own by-product of play advancing it.
The ten-minute balloon bonus and the five-level Cheese Rally race each set a bounded objective inside a short window, won or lost within that window rather than carried forward.
Cheese Rally states the player's own position against four named racers by progress toward five won levels, deciding who reaches the stage prize first, without showing the racers' own order.
Daily Goodies pays a four-week sequence of rewards for visiting once a day, framed entirely around the visit itself rather than any action taken once inside.
A bones meter fills with consecutive won levels in the same run of play and is separately kept in the profile as the longest win streak reached.
Player level and farm level each withhold a named set of features, power-ups, multipliers, My Trail, the Social Hub, the Grand Album and teams, stated and shown as locked before the level is reached.

Reaching level 10, 25 and 50 is recognized with its own congratulation and a gift held apart from the level's ordinary win reward.
An invite link ties a reward to a friend joining and reaching level 15, credited to the inviting user once that happens.

connections.title: The stake scales every reward at once
connections.desc: The multiplier raises both the level's entry cost and every reward it pays, credits, gems, cookies, puzzle pieces and pack quality, together.
connections.effect: The single per-level stake decision is also a decision about the speed of every other balance in the game.

connections.title: The stake decides the pack color
connections.desc: The card pack awarded for winning a level is green at one-times, blue at two-times and purple at four-times.
connections.effect: Betting higher is also a decision about the tier of pack the level's free draw can produce.

connections.title: Daily Goodies is a free credit faucet
connections.desc: Daily Goodies pays credits and items on a four-week sequence for visiting once a day.
connections.effect: The daily reward is one of a wide set of free routes into the same balance the level loop already funds.

connections.title: Trail and puzzle rewards pay credits
connections.desc: My Trail and the Grand Puzzle both pay credits along their reward positions.
connections.effect: Progress on either track feeds the same balance a level entry spends.

connections.title: Set rewards pay credits
connections.desc: Completing a set in the Grand Spring Album pays a credit reward between 8,000 and 40,000.
connections.effect: Album progress is also a credit faucet, not just a collection goal.

connections.title: The free wheel spin pays credits
connections.desc: The free lucky wheel spin resolves to one of several prizes, most of them credit amounts.
connections.effect: A free draw with no entry cost still feeds the same balance every other system spends.

connections.title: The store and every timed offer sell into the same balance
connections.desc: The timed offers, the store, the Grand Kit, the paid wheel spin and the puzzle piece sale all sell credits, gems, free rounds or puzzle pieces.
connections.effect: Every purchase surface in the game refills the same handful of balances the level loop already produces for free.

connections.title: The paid wheel spin is a purchase
connections.desc: The second lucky wheel spin costs 2.99 and resolves only after payment.
connections.effect: Money buys the draw itself, not just a chance at a better prize pool.

connections.title: The album is also sold in the store
connections.desc: From level 36, store bundles include the same card packs the album is filled from.
connections.effect: A player short on packs from play can buy directly into album progress.

connections.title: Bundles are built from held items
connections.desc: Store bundles and timed offers include power-ups and assist items, undos, wild cards and plus-five stacks, alongside credits.
connections.effect: Buying a bundle restocks the same held items rewards and level gifts already grant for free.

connections.title: Every level played fills Peggy
connections.desc: Peggy adds a bonus deposit after every level played, won or lost, drawn from the app's own contribution rather than the player's balance.
connections.effect: Simply playing, regardless of outcome, fills a reserve the player doesn't yet control.

connections.title: Claiming Peggy is a purchase
connections.desc: Once capped at 35,000 credits, Peggy can only be released for a 3.99 payment.
connections.effect: A reserve built entirely for free converts into a single, fixed-price purchase decision.

connections.title: Farm tasks are paid for in gems and grant XP
connections.desc: Completing a farm restoration task costs gems and pays XP toward the farm's next level.
connections.effect: Spending one earned balance is what produces progress on a completely different track.

connections.title: Farm XP raises the farm's level
connections.desc: The farm announces reaching level one and then level two as XP from tasks accumulates.
connections.effect: The farm's own progression state is a direct function of the XP its tasks pay out.

connections.title: Player and farm level decide what opens next
connections.desc: Power-ups, multipliers, My Trail, the Social Hub, the Grand Album and teams each name a player level; the farm withholds areas until its own level rises.
connections.effect: Two separate leveling tracks are what every stated gate in the game actually reads.

connections.title: Trail energy is what advances My Trail
connections.desc: My Trail's ten reward positions are advanced by energy paid out from completing missions.
connections.effect: The trail's own progression is entirely a function of the mission-earned resource feeding it.

connections.title: Packs won from levels fill the album
connections.desc: The Grand Spring Album is filled by packs won from levels and opened afterward.
connections.effect: A free, no-cost draw is the primary route into a collection the game also sells access to.

connections.title: The same race backs both the objective and the rank
connections.desc: Cheese Rally sets a bounded five-level objective and simultaneously states the player's own position against four named racers, without showing their full order.
connections.effect: One event produces both a pass-or-fail outcome and a live stated standing.
